perspective: Security engineer discovering artifacts on an endpoint
result: 85 benign roots have zero suspicious or hostile findings; four malicious roots each have two hostile findings in distinct directories and were relocated after verification.
malicious_evidence: All four malformed GIF carriers conceal validated 32-bit Windows PE images under repeating XOR, starting at byte 13.
163eda7f8382 allocates executable memory, receives into the same buffer, calls CryptDecrypt on it, and invokes that same saved pointer. Static IAT and frame-slot checks bind these operations.
The other three contain bounded length-prefixed NRV2B-8 streams. Static recovery yields complete PE command backdoors with the classic MiniDuke command/response dialect and custom wire alphabet.
Changing XOR keys, sample names, and command server strings preserves detection. Breaking the socket, decryption, allocation, or same-buffer call relation removes the execution finding.
No samples were executed. ML verdicts were not used as classification evidence.
benign_evidence: All 76 standalone image streams passed a strict GIF block walk and bounded libgif decoding of every frame, including palette and canvas bounds checks. First/middle/last coalesced frames were visually reviewed.
Screen recordings called exploit.gif and fileless-xec.gif contain raster demonstrations, not executable content.

Nine archives are recognizable software/source distributions. Every archive received recursive scanning; flagged members were extracted and inspected separately. Their flags came from ordinary source/configuration/documentation behavior.

The 20 archive GIF members include intentionally malformed image-library regression inputs, UTF-8-damaged icons, concatenated image test data and a missing-trailer UI icon. The complete animation was decoded and viewed; partial or invalid samples were bounded and statically inspected. They contain no recovered PE or request-driven PHP payload.
Archive labels describe the reviewed package, and do not authorize labeling arbitrary standalone malformed inputs as benign.
additional_accuracy_fixes: The JS filename quote-breakout matcher now requires the literal as an actual exec/execSync argument; a changelog parsed as JavaScript is not an execution sink.
Python empty display-method observations use parsed return expressions and exclude nonempty triple-quoted strings.
PHP auto-file assignments require a nonempty quoted or unquoted value. Empty settings are not selected files.
Removed the invisible-name-only conviction: existing raw function facts retain that spelling without inferring hiding.
Executable hyperlinks are neutral destinations. An ordinary PDF annotation plus an executable URL does not prove a hostile lure.
NRV decompression is a notable format observation. Malicious intent comes from child analysis.

classification_recording.reason: Skill requires make validate to pass before recording classifications. Global validation is still blocked. Four local malicious relocations are complete; 89 Hopper rulings remain pending.
classification_recording.required_skill_quote: Once atomscan shows the desired results, ensure that `make validate` passes, then use `hopper mv -target=<label> <sha256>` to record the classification and move the sample into its matching pool.

deployment_note: The rules require both the filefacts GIF XOR recovery patch and the cleave bounded NRV8 recovery patch. Sibling source edits and builds are present locally; patches are retained here. No commits or pushes were made by this task.
